configs.description: CCR2116-12G-4S+ - twelve gigabit Ethernet jacks, four SFP+ cages, a gigabit management jack, an RJ45 console and a USB 3.0 type A port, with two AC supplies and four fans (all part of the chassis in this model). The box holds two power cords, rack ears and a fastening set.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: No dimensions drawing is held; the front is read off studio photograph 2625, which looks slightly down, so x is photo-measured and y is estimated.
No rear view is held; the rear is read off studio photograph 2116, which looks down on it, so the y positions are estimated.

The brochure gives 72 W maximum and 60 W without attachments; the product page gives 83 W maximum and 60 W without attachments. The brochure's are carried and the page's maximum is kept as power-max-w-page. The brochure's "Power adapter nominal voltage 12 V" and "nominal current 10.8 A" are the adapter's nominal figures, filed as such and not as the box's input.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of the maximum consumption.

gaps.note: The page says "Number of PSU slots 2", the brochure says a dual-redundant power supply is included, and no held document prints a supply part number or shows a module. The two supplies are part of the chassis with their inlets and no bay is added; the base configuration exports two power ports.
gaps.wanted: The supply's part number and a statement of what a slot holds.

gaps.note: The page says 4 fans and the rear photograph shows five round openings. The four in the right half are fans; the fifth, between the inlets, is drawn as a vent. No document says what it is, and none states a fan redundancy form.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's fan count and the opening's purpose.

gaps.note: The brochure lists "Number of M.2 slots 1". No photograph shows an M.2 slot on either face, so it is internal: nothing is drawn and no port is added for it, and the export carries no interface for it.
gaps.wanted: A statement of where the slot is reached.

gaps.note: Searched the brochure, the page and the quick guide page for an LED table: none. The lamps carry the component's own vocabulary and no meaning is stated. The lamps' resting colour comes from the lamp component, not from this device: the photograph shows the jack lamps lit green and amber and the four status lamps lit green, red and blue, and a still render draws the component's own resting colour. It is not changed here.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's LED description for the CCR2116-12G-4S+.

gaps.note: Photographs 2625, 2629 and 2632 show a plain lid with embossed lettering; no document shows the underside.
gaps.wanted: A top and a bottom view.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The brochure says "a dual-redundant power supply" and "Number of AC inputs 2"; the page says "Number of AC inputs 2" and "Number of PSU slots 2". No held document prints a supply part number and photograph 2116 shows two plain C14 inlets with wire clips and no module, handle or latch, so the supplies are part of the chassis with their inlets and no bay is drawn. The page says "Cooling type 4 fans" and the photograph shows five round openings: the four in the right half are the fans, and the fifth, between the inlets, is drawn as a vent.

chassis.note: 443 x 199 x 44 mm: the brochure and the product page print the same figures. The width is the full ear-to-ear width as printed (the ears ship flush). No drawing is held, so it cannot be checked whether the 199 includes what stands off the rear: the two wire retaining clips of the inlets stand off the lid at the rear edge in photographs 2629 and 2632, and the depth is carried as printed, taken as the body with the retaining clips not counted (assumed, not measured).

colour.note: The front face is drawn #dddddd, the median of photograph 2625 and the brochure's front figure within 2 levels (the samples are under colour-sample). The rear is one device with the front's colour, but it reads darker in the rear photograph, so a panel rect paints the whole rear face #c1c1c0 under the inlets and grilles, and the five hubs match it. Chosen from three plain patches of photograph 2116 away from the inlets, fans, text, screws and the shaded edges: x 1150 to 1500, y 960 to 1060 (35000 pixels, median #c0bfbf), x 2850 to 3200, y 960 to 1060 (35000 pixels, #c4c4c4) and x 2850 to 3200, y 930 to 955 (8750 pixels, #c1c1c0), whose joint median over 78750 pixels is #c1c1c0 (the patches' medians span #c0bfbf to #c4c4c4: the photograph is lit from the right). The community NetBox rear elevation, an artist's flat render in the artist's own palette, reads #c0c0c0 over 48000 pixels of three plain patches, and is not used.

colour-sample.note: Face #dddddd: the median of 68600 pixels of photograph 2625 over x 2485 to 2975, y 980 to 1120 (plain face right of the lamp legends) is #dbdbde, and of 17000 pixels of the brochure's front figure (fig. 5) over x 1010 to 1210, y 130 to 215 is #dbdbde: within 2 levels of #dddddd, which is kept. The jack plates #c4c4c4: the median of 540 pixels of photograph 2625 over x 1010 to 1100, y 998 to 1004 (the plate's top strip) is #bec0c8, within 6 levels. The rear is lit less and reads darker, so it is painted its own colour (see colour). The lamps' colours belong to the component skins and are not changed here. The jack plates and the outlines round them are under front-outlines.

datasheet.note: Brochure specifications: product code CCR2116-12G-4S+, AL73400 2 GHz ARM 64 bit, 16 cores, 16 GB DDR4, 128 MB NAND, 13 gigabit Ethernet ports, 4 SFP+ ports, 1 M.2 slot, 1 USB 3.0 type A, 98DX3255 switch chip, 443 x 199 x 44 mm, -20 to +60 C; powering 2 AC inputs, 100-240 V, adapter nominal 12 V and 10.8 A, 60 W without attachments, 72 W maximum; included: 2 power cords, rackmount bracket white, fastening set.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (brochure: Rackmount bracket white; page: the same). They ship flush with the face and are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From photograph 2625 at 4.01 px per mm. SFP+ cages: left column centre 15.2 mm, right 30.4 mm, upper cages top at 11.7 mm and lower at 27.3 mm (a 15.6 mm row pitch). Jacks: 16.5 mm frames on a 17.0 mm pitch, jack top at 25.6 mm, in three plates of four at gutters of 4.2 mm. The console and management jacks sit in one 17.2 x 27.4 mm plate at 258.9 mm, USB at 282.5 mm, MODE at 291.4 mm and RESET at 301.4 mm. Colours: see colour-sample.

front-outlines.note: Read on photograph 2625 at 7.092 px per mm. Each block of four jacks and the console and management pair are ringed in black and each jack's own frame is light: the black is a rectangle of the block's extent (#010101, the median of 300 pixels between two frames at x 608 to 613, y 1015 to 1075), and a light plate 15.5 x 12.4 mm sits over it behind each jack, #bbbec3 (the median of 720 pixels of the plate's top strip at x 515 to 595, y 999 to 1008), which leaves the black 0.75 mm round a block and 1.6 mm between two jacks. The console and management pair has a 17.2 mm black outline (#040404, the median of 140 pixels at x 2007 to 2009, y 1010 to 1080) round a plain plate of the face's own colour, #dedddf (900 pixels at x 2040 to 2100, y 995 to 1010). The jack component's own face is narrower than the photograph's frame, so the plate behind it carries the frame's width. The four SFP+ cages stand on one black backing of their block's extent with a margin of 0.6 mm (#010101), with the light strip between the two rows of cages, #b9b9bd (the median of 160 pixels at x 275 to 285, y 984 to 1000), over it; the bracket printed at its left is two 0.2 mm strokes with a gap for the SFP+ label.

gate-1.note: No drawing is held. Photograph 2625's body is 1777 px across at the displayed 2000 px width for the printed 443 (4.01 px per mm); x is taken at that scale from the body's left edge. The photograph looks slightly down, so the face is foreshortened by about 5 percent: y is measured up from the face's bottom edge at 44 mm for the face and is estimated. The jack pitch reads 68.2 px = 17.0 mm on three gangs, and the same 17.0 mm across the three blocks' twelve jacks (first centres 51.4, 123.5 and 195.8 mm) on a quantity the scale never saw.

lamps.note: Each jack carries its own two small lamps (the component's, green at the left and amber at the right in the photograph). The eight arrows between the SFP+ cages are read as four to a stack, two per cage, as the CRS518's: down for the lower cage and up for the upper, estimated from the photograph. The four chassis lamps (USER, FAULT, PWR 2, PWR 1) are at 309.7 mm, 18.8 to 33.5 mm down. No held document says what a lamp shows.

legends.note: The legends are set at 2.2 mm. Each cap height was read on its photograph: USER, CONSOLE, ETH/BOOT and MODE on photograph 2625 are 11 to 14 px tall at 7.092 px per mm, 1.6 to 1.9 mm of cap (a 2.2 to 2.6 mm font), and the face's wider letter shapes fix the size by width: USER is 41 px, 5.8 mm, the same as DejaVu at 2.2 mm. The rear's POWER and rating lines on photograph 2116 are 11 to 12 px tall at 7.16 px per mm and the rating line 247 px, 34.5 mm, across, which 2.2 mm also draws. The model text keeps 2.8 mm.

port-numbering.note: Jacks 1 to 12 are printed under the jacks, left to right, under GIGABIT ETHERNET. The SFP+ cages print 1 and 3 under the stacks and 2 and 4 over them, so the lower cage of a stack is odd. ETH/BOOT is printed under the lower of the two stacked jacks and CONSOLE over the upper, so the management jack (the brochure's thirteenth gigabit port) is the lower one and the console the upper.

rear-holes.note: estimated - photograph 2116 shows two dark round holes at the upper-left and lower-right corners of the fifth opening, and the NetBox rear elevation shows them too. Read on a 3x crop at 7.16 px per mm: each is 28 px, 3.9 mm, across (606 and 589 dark pixels, centres at x 563 and 799, y 891 and 1113), 16.5 mm left or right and 16.7 mm above or below the opening's centre (the camera looks down, so the vertical figure is estimated at 6.65 px per mm). Drawn as two round decor rects filled #1b1b1a, the median of 200 pixels over both holes; the photograph's lighter countersink ring is not drawn.

rear-layout.note: estimated - no rear elevation is held; the positions are read off photograph 2116 (body 1885 px across a 1.05 scaled crop, 4.255 px per mm) and the NetBox rear elevation agrees on every opening. It looks down on the rear, so x is good to about 1.5 mm and y, from the face's bottom edge, to about 2.5 mm. Inlets at 30.9 and 116.3 mm, each with POWER 1 or 2 and the rating line under it; round openings at 72.4, 223.7, 264.4, 304.4 and 345.0 mm, 37 mm across. The five guards are honeycombs, hexagonal holes round a plain hub in photograph 2116 and the NetBox rear elevation. Read on photograph 2116 at 7.16 px per mm (the body's 3172 px at 3500 px width) in a 3x crop of the fourth fan: hexagons 5.4 mm across corners and 4.56 across flats, 5.1 mm between columns and 5.86 mm centre to centre down one, with a hexagon at the hub's centre and one whole ring cut by the opening's circle (the fifth guard is read as the same lattice, estimated). Drawn as `motif`, one tile of two columns (10.184 x 5.88 mm) holding hexagons 5.36 mm across corners, the tile's origin at each guard's centre. The plain `vent` pattern ties the hexagon to its pitch: scaled to this 5.88 mm pitch its web is 0.8 mm where the photograph's is about 1.3, so it draws the metal too fat. The inlets' wire retaining clips and the screws are not drawn (no registry part).

side-layout.note: Photograph 2632 shows the right wall with a field of round perforations at the rear half of the wall; it is read as a 100 x 22 mm field starting 66 mm from the front, estimated to about 10 mm because the wall is foreshortened. The perforations are small round holes in staggered rows, so the field is drawn with `holes` (round) and not `vent` (hexagons) at that pattern's own tile; the hole pitch cannot be read at that angle and is not measured. Photograph 2629 shows the left wall plain, with screws and a few holes.

vent-band.note: estimated - measured on photograph 2625 at 7.092 px per mm (the body's 3142 px, 175 to 3317 at its original 3500 px width, for the printed 443 mm) across, and for y from the face's bottom edge at the same scale as the jacks (the camera looks slightly down). The band is a chain of slanted strokes at 45 degrees, each 2.0 mm across and 6.8 mm tall, repeating every 31.2 mm (221.4 px): a V (two strokes, their tops 11.5 mm apart), a single "/", a lambda (the V upside down, its apex 22.3 mm from the V's left stroke) and a single "\". It runs from 44.3 mm (px 489) to 255.0 mm (px 1983), 210.7 mm: six periods and 0.7 of a seventh, so seven V points and six lambdas. The left end is cut vertically through the foot of the lambda's right stroke (2.95 mm of it is left), and the right end through the head of a single stroke. The V and the lambda come to a point here; the metal rounds each point to about 1.3 mm. Drawn as one `motif` field, tile 31.2 x 7.0 mm, five cells (the lambda is cut where it crosses the tile's right edge and its foot reappears at the left), the tile's origin at the field's left edge. The tile is 7.0 mm tall, 0.2 mm more than the strokes, with every cell 0.1 mm inside its top and bottom edges and the tile begun 0.1 mm above the field: a cell on a tile edge left a faint 1 px seam between the strokes along it. No existing pattern draws slanted strokes.
